title: Refactor ops utility surface for modular runbook tasks and automated support flows
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood's oncall and first-line support teams maintain a large corpus of ad-hoc admin scripts and prose runbooks. These have drifted: multiple copies of the same steps, differing parameter sets, and limited telemetry. This ticket is to refactor the ops utility surface into composable, versioned task primitives and a deterministic runbook executor that can be orchestrated from the Console and invoked by the support CLI.

Goals:
- Convert the top 40 most-used admin scripts into typed, idempotent task primitives (atomic ops with clear inputs/outputs).
- Implement a deterministic runbook executor service (runbook-as-series-of-tasks) that supports checkpointing, dry-run, rollout percentages, and safe rollback hooks.
- Add structured telemetry (per-step latency, error counts, invoked parameters) and provenance (who triggered, which version of task/runbook).
- Expose: (1) a callable API for Console and CLI; (2) a safe default policy that requires approvers for high-impact steps.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire runbook corpus. We will prioritize the most frequently invoked, highest-severity recipes.
- Replacing external incident tooling—this integrates via webhooks and exports.

Acceptance criteria:
- 40 admin scripts rewritten to task primitives with unit tests and type schemas.
- Runbook executor deployed to staging with checkpointing and dry-run mode verified by SRE team.
- Telemetry dashboard (Console) shows per-step success rate and median latency.
- RBAC gating works for high-impact steps and is enforced by KMS-signed approvals.
- Migration plan documented and one customer-facing incident successfully remediated end-to-end using the new flow.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Task primitives will be small (single responsibility) to simplify rollback; this increases number of steps per runbook but reduces blast radius.
- Checkpointing will be implemented as idempotent markers in the runbook state store (etcd-backed). We opted for a simple state machine to reduce complexity vs. full workflow engine.
- Safety: high-risk tasks require a 2-person approval (approver + operator) and signing via KMS. This adds latency; mitigations: allow pre-approved scheduled windows and ephemeral elevated sessions.
- Performance: planner will prefer parallelizable steps but will never run dependent steps concurrently. Initial implementation focuses on correctness; we'll optimize batching of idempotent read-only primitives later.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Inventory: finalize top-40 scripts and map inputs/outputs (infra runbook spreadsheet -> design doc).
2) Task SDK: small Go/TS SDK for declaring tasks, schemas, and local dry-run harness.
3) Executor: service + HTTP API supporting create-execution, step-status, cancel, dry-run.
4) Console integration: UI to author runbooks by composing tasks, run, and view telemetry.
5) Telemetry & audit: emit structured events to our telemetry pipeline (Grafana/ClickHouse) and archive runbook provenance in audit logs.
6) Migration: staged migration with shadowing (run new executor in parallel, compare outputs) then cutover.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/1987654/ops-task-primitives-and-executor
- Inventory spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-admin-inventory
- Proto & SDK repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-task-sdk (WIP branch: feat/task-primitives)
- Executor prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/executor/pull/412

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for each task primitive and integration tests for runbook sequences.
- Staging: runbook dry-run against synthetic clusters; SRE to validate checkpointing semantics.
- Canary rollout: start with internal support team only (10% of ops), then 50%, then 100% over 2 weeks while monitoring safety signals.
- Rollback plan: ability to cancel execution and replay from last checkpoint; emergency fallout remediation runbook documented.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Fraction of incidents remediated via automated runbooks (target 30% within 3 months).
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for runbook-invoked fixes (target 25% reduction).
- Per-step failure rate (target <1% for stable primitives).

Security & compliance:
- KMS-backed signatures on approver actions.
- Full audit trail of inputs/outputs retained for 90 days.
- Security review required before production rollout.
